reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator 'phase_acceleration_signature' extracts interpretable movement features from 10 Hz Combine traces by isolating 0–1 second acceleration, which serves as a candidate signal for game-speed capacity. This is grounded in a dualism between static pre-draft metrics and dynamic game-time behavior. The operator assumes temporal locality and positional specificity, with breakdown occurring when post-snap bursts or non-linear motion dominate. The 'position_specific_repeatability' primitive acts as a derived kernel, filtering out noise by weighting acceleration features according to intra-class consistency. It ensures that only reliable signals propagate into downstream models. The 'game_speed_transfer_model' operates under an ablation framework, where early-phase acceleration is compared against late-phase and combined features to isolate predictive value. Failure modes arise when the model overfits to positional outliers or fails to control for play context such as alignment and blitz role. These primitives form a closed-loop system: raw kinematics → feature extraction → reliability assessment → predictive modeling — each layer refining the next.
